case_title: Kiriti Pal v. State of West Bengal
accused_occupation: Not stated (described only as posing as a teacher; a school official said no teacher of that name worked there)
accused_victim_relationship: Acquaintance (friendship and intimacy; A-1 frequently visited and was allowed to stay at the victim's residence)
statutory_provisions: IPC ss.302, 120B, 34, 376(2)(g); Arms Act ss.25, 27, 35 (charged). Convictions relevant to A-1: IPC ss.302, 120B; Arms Act s.25(1)(a)(b)
weapon: Improvised country-made single-shot pipe gun (recovered); wooden butts recovered; victim's neck tied with a saree
evidence_type: Circumstantial (last seen evidence, conduct, recovery of weapon, call records); medical evidence; witness testimony
confession: A-1 confessional statement led to seizure of motorcycle (relied on as recovery). A-2 and A-3 confessions led to recoveries (not sufficient to convict). A-4 judicial confession under s.164 Cr.P.C. held not inculpatory and insufficient alone
aggravating_circumstances: Victim strangled with saree and tied to a tree in an isolated jungle about 25 km from her home; head injuries; injury consistent with forcible intercourse; subsequent threats to witnesses
trial_court_outcome: A-1 to A-3 convicted under s.302 IPC and sentenced to death; also convicted under s.376(2)(g) IPC (life) and s.120B (life for all four accused); Arms Act s.25 three years for A-1 to A-3; A-4 life under s.120B
high_court_outcome: Partly allowed: s.376(2)(g) conviction set aside; s.302 death sentence modified to life imprisonment; A-4's s.120B conviction and life sentence confirmed; A-1 to A-3 conviction under s.302 upheld
offence_finally_established: Murder (IPC s.302) and criminal conspiracy (IPC s.120B) and Arms Act s.25(1)(a)(b), for A-1 only
neutral_facts: The victim, a widow who ran a beauty parlour, had become acquainted with one of the accused, and the two developed a close friendship; that accused frequently visited the victim's home and sometimes stayed overnight there. On an evening in November, the victim left home as a pillion rider on the motorcycle of that accused, telling a tenant she was going to a school function. The tenant later saw the accused return alone around 10 to 10:30 p.m. and, when asked about the victim, was told the victim was engaged with someone and would be brought back later. A school official testified that no function had been scheduled at that school on that date. The next morning the victim's body was found in an isolated jungle about 25 km from the residence, with the neck tied by one end of a saree whose other end was tied to a tree. The post-mortem found lacerated head wounds sufficient to cause death, and an injury consistent with forcible intercourse. Investigators arrested the accused, and on the basis of a confessional statement by one accused a motorcycle was seized. Recoveries of an improvised pipe gun with wooden butts were made from near a river and the jungle, and blood was detected on the butts. Call records showed numerous calls between the accused, and a notebook belonging to a co-accused contained a coded number of one accused. A witness testified that one accused threatened him and another witness not to disclose anything to the police.
physical_harm: Death by ligature (saree tied around neck) with lacerated head wounds and other injuries, including injury in the labia minora
number_of_offences: 7 charged (IPC ss.302, 120B, 34, 376(2)(g); Arms Act ss.25, 27, 35) for A-1; 3 finally upheld for A-1 (IPC ss.302, 120B; Arms Act s.25)
premeditation_planning: Not established: the court found telephone calls alone insufficient to prove conspiracy, and no separate finding of premeditation was made
motive: Not identified (the court accepted that absence of proved motive does not defeat the case, noting the mental disposition need not be proved)
key_evidence_accepted: Last-seen evidence of PWs 6, 7 and 10; A-1's failure to explain under s.106 Evidence Act; threats by A-1 to A-4 and PW7 (subsequent conduct); recovery of pipe gun and wooden butts at A-1's instance; blood detected on butts; medical evidence (PW29); intimacy between A-1 and victim
witness_credibility: PWs 6, 7 and 10 accepted as establishing last-seen and conduct facts; PW17 found far from convincing; PW11 noted that no teacher named A-1 worked at the school
post_offence_conduct: A-1 threatened A-4 by phone not to disclose facts of the murder to CID police and threatened PW7 not to disclose anything and to vacate the premises; court held this indicated A-1's nexus with the offence
trial_duration: offence: 11.11.2008; trial judgment: 26.7.2011 and 29.7.2011; High Court: 20.06.2012; Supreme Court: 16.04.2015
legal_representation: Accused: E. R. Sumathy (AC.), Sunil Kumar Jain, Parmatma Jain, Kaushik Chaudhary, Pawanshree Agrawal. State: Chanchal Kumar Ganguli, Kabir Shankar Bose, Narmada, Saakaar Sardana, Anip Sachthey
investigation_status: FIR registered (Sadaipur P.S. Case No.74/2008); inquest and post-mortem conducted; arrests made; further investigation by CID; charge sheet filed
procedural_irregularity: Recovery seizure list witness PW17 signed without knowing why; gold ring and silver chain not shown to other witnesses for identification
appeal_history: Trial court: A-1 to A-3 convicted (s.302 death, s.376(2)(g), s.120B, Arms Act); A-4 convicted under s.120B (life). High Court: partly allowed; s.376(2)(g) set aside; death modified to life; A-4 conviction confirmed. Supreme Court: A-1 appeal dismissed; A-2 to A-4 appeals allowed and acquitted
prosecution_argument: A-1 last seen with the victim and failed to explain how and when he parted company, so s.106 burden unmet; supported by threats to witnesses, recovery of the weapon at A-1's instance and call records
defence_argument: No motive attributed to A-1; friendship and intimacy alone insufficient to convict, so the courts below erred
legal_principle_applied: Last-seen theory with burden on the accused to explain under s.106 Evidence Act; circumstantial evidence must form a complete chain consistent only with guilt; motive is relevant but its absence is not automatically fatal
precedent_relied_upon: State of U.P. v. Satish (2005) 3 SCC 114; State of Rajasthan v. Kashi Ram (2006) 12 SCC 254; Vivek Kalra v. State of Rajasthan (2014) 12 SCC 439; Geejaganda Somaiah v. State of Karnataka (2007) 9 SCC 315 (referred)
sentencing_rationale: Not applicable (the Supreme Court confirmed the High Court's life sentence without separate sentencing reasoning)
other_sentence_order: None (beyond confirming A-1's conviction and sentence; A-2 to A-4 directed to be set at liberty if not required in any other case)
